Spatial Operators

class ibfs.spatial_operators.SpatialOperators(Re)[source]

Bases: object

Class to evaluate the right-hand side of the Navier-Stokes equation.

evaluate_advective_term_x(u: array, v: array) → array[source]

Compute

\[\int_{Y} u^2(x,y)\big\lvert_{x=x_{l}}^{x=x_r}\,dy + \int_{X}\left[u(x,y)v(x,y)\right]_{y={y_b}}^{y=y_{t}}\,dx\]
evaluate_derivative(mesh, w: array, order: int, axis: int)[source]

Evaluate derivative of field \(w\) in the direction specified by axis. The order of the derivative (i.e., first or second) is specified by order.

Parameters:

  • w (numpy/cupy array) – two-dimensional array

  • order (int) – order of the derivative

  • axis (int) – direction along which to take the derivative

Return type:

numpy/cupy array

evaluate_viscous_term(w: array) → array[source]

Compute

\[Re^{-1}\nabla^2 w = Re^{-1}\left(\partial_x^2 w + \partial_y^2 w\right)\]

where \(w\) is either the \(x\) or \(y\) velocity field.

Parameters:

w (numpy/cupy array) – two-dimensional array

Attention

This function returns an array of a different size than the original input array \(w\). If \(w\) has size \(n\times m\), the dimension of the output array will be \((n-2)\times (m-2)\).

Return type:

cupy/numpy array

interpolate_1d(w: array, axis: int) → array[source]

Perform 1d interpolation of the two-dimensional array \(w\) along the direction specified by axis.

Parameters:

  • w (numpy/cupy array) – two-dimensional array we wish to interpolate

  • axis (int) – direction of interpolation

Attention

This function returns an array of a different size than the original input array \(w\). If \(w\) has size \(n\times m\), the dimension along axis is reduced by \(1\).

Return type:

numpy/cupy array

interpolate_2d(w: array) → array[source]

Apply interpolate_1d() twice along both directions.

Parameters:

w (numpy/cupy array) – two-dimensional array we wish to interpolate

Attention

This function returns an array of a different size than the original input array \(w\). If \(w\) has size \(n\times m\), the dimension of the output array will be \((n-1)\times (m-1)\).

Return type:

numpy/cupy array
